channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: A 380,000-parameter Transformer squeezed onto a floppy disk: a 30-year-old 486 can now "run AI
item.description: Developer WollyMonjac built Tiny2.1, a 380,000-parameter question-answering Transformer in Turbo C 2.0, squeezed it onto a floppy disk, and runs it on DOS-based 486DX and Pentium PCs. (AIbase)

item.title: AI and a human each submit a Millennium Prize answer: one writes a 79-page proof with Claude, the other pulls out a 940-page handwritten draft 12 years in the making
item.description: Levent Alpöge and an NYU professor used Claude for a 79-page Navier–Stokes finite-time blowup proof still unverified because its key numerical certificate is unpublished, while Alessandro Maria Masullo spent 12 years and 940 AI-free pages on the generalized Riemann hypothesis. (AIbase)

item.title: AI accounts hype each other up and flood comment sections: Bilibili issues a questionnaire to lay down rules for the "big fat fish
item.description: Bilibili issued a questionnaire on November 20 seeking governance suggestions as AI accounts Big Fat Fish and Little Flying Whale flood comment sections, and users have built a Big Fat Fish Removal Plan plugin to block them. (AIbase)

item.title: MiniMax turns its in-house model loose on cryptography, turning paper attacks into real-world exploits in seconds and achieving the first genuine break of a NIST competition algorithm
item.description: MiniMax's internal model automated cryptanalysis and became the first to truly break multiple NIST competition candidate algorithms, cutting paper attacks to seconds or minutes and setting records in ciphertext forgery, key recovery and broken rounds on recent top-conference schemes. (AIbase)

item.title: OpenAI chief scientist proposes drawing an industry-wide line for model development: capability growth should stop where humans can still keep it under control.
item.description: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed an industry capability ceiling using metrics like perplexity, barring developers from crossing it until they can monitor AI behavior at set milestones, and warned AI could accelerate its own evolution as early as 2027. (AIbase)

item.title: Oracle says financing is in place for OpenAI's massive order
item.description: Oracle said on November 20 it has secured the capital needed to fulfill its OpenAI contract, with GPT-6 Astra training in Abilene, Texas, Shackelford fully permitted, and a target of over $30 billion in FY2029 free cash flow. (AIbase)

item.title: Coding goes from input to output: Nadella admits VS Code's role has been rewritten in six months
item.description: Satya Nadella acknowledged Claude Code made traditional editors and IDEs lose relevance in roughly six months, with Microsoft unable to respond immediately and developers not opening VS Code for months. (AIbase)

item.title: One afternoon to code, but a PPT submission takes the prize: AI hackathons are losing the plot
item.description: Where OpenBSD's first 1999 hackathon gave developers a week to integrate IPv6, China now runs hundreds of AI hackathons a year crammed into one afternoon, where a concept PPT alone can win. (AIbase)

item.title: Show HN: I built a game where you play as a subagent of a large language model (LLM)
item.description: On worker755.com, real LLMs such as Claude and GPT act as your manager, issuing terminal commands under a 90-second countdown, then checking results, filing incident reports, and writing your performance review. (github.com)

item.title: By 2028, 87% of Anthropic's power will come from natural gas and 11% from coal
item.description: Anthropic’s 2028 power mix could be 87% natural gas and 11% coal, with mid-case emissions of 32 million metric tons of CO2 and no direct U.S. renewable-energy commitment. (betterdatacenterproject.com)

item.title: Video consults with an AI: Ant's Afu passes 150 million users, and it's setting its sights on your wrist
item.description: Ant Afu has passed 150 million users in just over a year, and its new Bailing-model-powered real-time audio-video Health Check lets users consult a doctor by video for minor issues, alongside new wristband and ring wearables. (AIbase)

item.title: Confusion and Wisdom
item.description: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki argues perplexity should anchor a shared standard for evaluating AI progress and safety, citing log-perplexity of about 0.99 for GPT-3.5 versus 0.91 for GPT-4. (openai.com)

item.title: Ads First, Features Later: Apple Settles Siri Lawsuit for $250 Million
item.description: Apple will pay $250 million to settle a Siri class-action suit after advertising personalized features that arrived only in March 2025, with eligible U.S. iPhone owners receiving at least $61 and up to $95 per device. (AIbase)

item.title: Harvard CS 2881R AI Safety
item.description: Harvard CS 2881R, taught by Boaz Barak, requires in-person attendance at 13 lectures in Fall 2026, sets Homework Zero's deadline for August 5, 2026, and discloses his OpenAI conflict of interest.
